title: Effect of hot deformation on bainitic transformation and retained austenite in a 3Mn medium Mn steel
abstract: This study aimed to explore how deformed austenite affected the carbide-free bainitic transformation in a Fe-3Mn-0.2C-1.5Si medium Mn steel (MMnS). The MMnS was firstly subjected to high-temperature deformation using a Gleeble-3500 thermomechanical simulator, followed by isothermal soaking for bainitic transformation. The results revealed that the states of austenite, whether recrystallized or not, significantly influenced the morphology of the resulting bainitic microstructures. Granular-like bainite was found preferentially nucleated and grew within the recrystallized austenite grains, while lath-like bainite formed in unrecrystallized regions, where its development was significantly influenced by deformation-induced substructures. These substructures served as heterogenous nucleation sites for the lath-like bainite, resulting in its distinctive intersected morphology. A higher volume fraction of retained austenite with finer grain size was achieved in the final microstructures. This study provided new insights into the mechanisms of bainitic transformation in the deformed austenite, offering a novel approach for tailoring the mechanical performance of MMnSs.
